checks.title: Pinned commit identity
checks.hypothesis: The audited tree is exactly postfiatd commit 0085a1ff885d6a446369cf73a4430f75af22be55.

checks.title: ML-KEM / Kyber absent from the pinned tree
checks.hypothesis: No file in the pinned tree mentions ML-KEM, MLKEM, or Kyber: there is no ML-KEM code to migrate from, only code to add.

checks.title: X25519 and application-code ECDH absent
checks.hypothesis: The tree has no X25519 code anywhere and no ECDH call sites in the application code: the only ECDH hits are the vendored secp256k1 library and one research document.

checks.title: 'encapsulat*' hits in src/ are non-KEM prose
checks.hypothesis: The five 'encapsulat*' matches in src/ are ordinary English ('encapsulate a test env', 'encapsulates the DER identifier'), not key encapsulation; no KeyEncapsulation symbol exists in src/.

checks.title: Signing present: ed25519 / secp256k1 only
checks.hypothesis: The tree's asymmetric cryptography is signing only: ed25519 and secp256k1 appear across src/, and no key-exchange primitive does.

checks.title: TLS context construction is fully pinned
checks.hypothesis: The peer TLS context is built in src/libxrpl/basics/make_SSLContext.cpp with a fixed method (sslv23), a fixed cipher list, TLS 1.1 as the floor, a 2048-bit RSA ephemeral self-signed certificate, and fixed 2048-bit DH parameters.

checks.title: Peer connections use the anonymous TLS context
checks.hypothesis: OverlayImpl wires peer connections to make_SSLContext("") — the anonymous context with the ephemeral self-signed RSA certificate — and ConnectAttempt sets verify_none before the client handshake: X.509 authentication is not used on the peer path.

checks.title: No TLS group / curve / KEM configuration exists
checks.hypothesis: Nothing in the TLS setup or the overlay configures TLS groups, curves, or a KEM: there is no hook point where a hybrid group such as X25519MLKEM768 could be selected today.

checks.title: Node identity is always secp256k1
checks.hypothesis: The node identity keypair is derived from the [node_seed] seed (or the wallet DB) as secp256k1, unconditionally: a migration cannot reuse the node identity as a KEM key without changing this code.

checks.title: Overlay handshake requires a secp256k1 node key
checks.hypothesis: verifyHandshake rejects any node public key that is not secp256k1, and signDigest refuses to sign a digest with anything but secp256k1: ed25519 node identities cannot peer today.

checks.title: Session signature binds TLS finished messages
checks.hypothesis: The shared value signed in the overlay handshake is the XOR of the SHA-512 hashes of the local and peer TLS Finished messages, halved: it proves the peer holds the node key AND that the TLS session is end-to-end with that node.

checks.title: Validator keys come from config; no KEM section
checks.hypothesis: Validator keys are loaded from the [validator_token] config section at startup; no [kem] (or any KEM) config section exists, so a KEM key has nowhere to be configured today.

checks.title: No KEM key storage or persistence paths in the tree
checks.hypothesis: No file in the tree is named for a KEM, and no code path persists KEM key material: a migration introduces the first KEM key storage in the codebase, and its format is a fresh design decision.

checks.title: ML-KEM-512 sizes exact (FIPS 203 Table 3)
checks.hypothesis: liboqs reports ML-KEM-512 key/ciphertext/shared-secret lengths exactly as FIPS 203 Table 3 requires: ek 800, dk 1632, ct 768, ss 32 bytes.

checks.title: ML-KEM-768 sizes exact (FIPS 203 Table 3)
checks.hypothesis: liboqs and pyca/cryptography agree ML-KEM-768 is ek 1184, dk 2400, ct 1088, ss 32 bytes, exactly as FIPS 203 Table 3 requires.

checks.title: ML-KEM-1024 sizes exact (FIPS 203 Table 3)
checks.hypothesis: liboqs and pyca/cryptography agree ML-KEM-1024 is ek 1568, dk 3168, ct 1568, ss 32 bytes, exactly as FIPS 203 Table 3 requires.

checks.title: X25519 sizes exact (RFC 7748 section 5)
checks.hypothesis: X25519 public keys and shared secrets are 32 bytes each, per RFC 7748: the classical baseline the hybrid handshake must carry alongside the ML-KEM values.

checks.title: Hybrid wire overhead per parameter set
checks.hypothesis: A hybrid public key (32-byte X25519 key + ML-KEM encapsulation key) and hybrid ciphertext (32-byte X25519 key + ML-KEM ciphertext) are 25x/37x/49x (public key) and 24x/34x/49x (ciphertext) the classical 32-byte values.

checks.title: ML-KEM keygen timing, all parameter sets
checks.hypothesis: Key generation cost grows with the parameter set (512 < 768 < 1024) and stays in the sub-millisecond range on this machine.

checks.title: ML-KEM encapsulation timing, all parameter sets
checks.hypothesis: Encapsulation cost grows with the parameter set (512 < 768 < 1024).

checks.title: ML-KEM decapsulation timing, all parameter sets
checks.hypothesis: Decapsulation cost grows with the parameter set (512 < 768 < 1024).

checks.title: X25519 baseline timing (classical handshake)
checks.hypothesis: The classical X25519 baseline — two key generations and two exchanges, one per peer — is the floor the hybrid variants build on; the pure exchange cost is measured separately from key generation so the component sum does not double-count.

checks.title: Hybrid handshake total vs classical baseline
checks.hypothesis: The hybrid handshake costs only a small increment over the classical handshake (well under 20x for every parameter set): the ML-KEM operations add roughly 0.04-0.09 ms on top of the X25519 baseline, and the HKDF combiner is negligible next to both.

checks.title: HKDF combiner correctness and domain separation
checks.hypothesis: The hybrid combiner (HKDF-SHA256 over x25519_ss || mlkem_ss) is deterministic, produces 32-byte outputs, separates domains by info string, and changes output when either input changes.

checks.title: Impl C vs NIST ACVP known-answer vectors
checks.hypothesis: The pure-Python FIPS 203 implementation reproduces the NIST ACVP keyGen, encapsulation, and decapsulation vectors for all three parameter sets exactly, grounding every measurement in the standard itself.

checks.title: Cross-implementation agreement (A, B, C)
checks.hypothesis: Ciphertexts produced by one implementation decapsulate to the same shared secret in the others, for every parameter set: liboqs and pyca/cryptography agree with the standard-derived implementation on the wire format.

checks.title: Round-trip correctness, liboqs and pyca
checks.hypothesis: Encapsulate-then-decapsulate returns the same 32-byte shared secret for every parameter set in liboqs and (768/1024) in pyca/cryptography, over 25 fresh keypairs each.

checks.title: Negotiation matrix, exhaustive
checks.hypothesis: The negotiation model returns exactly the expected outcome for every (policy, peer offer) combination: 3 policies x 6 offer sets = 18 cells, checked against fixtures/negotiation_matrix.json.

checks.title: Downgrade detection via transcript hash
checks.hypothesis: Removing a hybrid algorithm from the offered list changes the negotiation transcript hash, so a downgrade attack in transit is detectable: the peer's transcript will not match the initiator's.

checks.title: Mismatched hybrid and classical-only outcomes
checks.hypothesis: A peer offering only ML-KEM-512 when the local policy requires 768 is rejected (fail closed); a classical-only peer is rejected under require-hybrid and accepted with a recorded downgrade event under prefer-hybrid.

checks.title: Fresh ephemeral keys per handshake
checks.hypothesis: One hundred hybrid handshakes generate one hundred distinct encapsulation keys and one hundred distinct shared secrets: a compromised session key exposes only that session.

checks.title: Key-compromise rotation maps to config-only steps
checks.hypothesis: Every rotation step for a compromised KEM key maps to a config change, an operator action, or a restart — no step requires a code change — because keys are loaded once at startup from configuration, exactly like the existing validator keys.

checks.title: Rollback to classical-only is policy-only
checks.hypothesis: Every rollback step is a policy or config change: no tree code is removed or changed, because the tree contains no KEM code to remove (K02) and the hybrid path lives outside the pinned tree until a migration lands.
